occurrenceRemarks: I need help identifying this grouper species captured in an estuary. The fish has 10 dorsal spines and 17 soft rays and the anal fin has 3 spines and 8 rays. It shows typical Epinephelus-like characters such as a rounded caudal fin and strong serrations on the preopercle and it closely resembles Epinephelus diacanthus. However, the meristic counts do not match perfectly, especially the dorsal spine number, which creates confusion in identification. I would appreciate any expert input on this.

occurrenceRemarks: Fringescale Sardinella is one of the expected Sardinella spp around or nearby Bay of Bengal territory. It's a short sized slender shaped Sardinella lives in sea, offshore, coastal lines and possibly breeds around coastline to estuaries. Particular specimen has collected from a coastal area of Barguna district, Bangladesh. Results from sample examination has given below. Dorsal Ray count: 17 Pectoral Ray: 15 Anal Soft Ray: 21 Lower Gill rackers: 48 Dark tail, bright pectoral, ventral and anal fins. Has an array of fringed scales on upper lateral. Production and Availability: It's probably a regular species found around during monsoon seasons due to availability of food sources and suitable water condition. Availability and conservation status of the species in Bay of Bengal region is in DD state. Needs more viable study in year round to assume a clear concept. Commercial importance: The fish is commercially important in coastal area. So it's conservation steps during breeding time should be taken carefully.
